exposure: Vaginal dinoprostone (gel or insert) for induction of labor
Obstetric disorders (e.g., gestational diabetes mellitus, hypertensive disorders)
cohort: The study included 1687 patients undergoing induction of labor with vaginal dinoprostone (gel or insert) between August 2019 and June 2022.
finding: The main adverse event associated with dinoprostone use was tachysystole, which was not linked to an increased risk of cesarean section, NICU admission, low 1-min Apgar, or umbilical cord acidosis; the study concluded dinoprostone can be safely administered for labor induction, even in high-risk pregnancies, with adequate surveillance.
mod_finding: Tachysystole, the main adverse event associated with dinoprostone, was not associated with an increased risk of cesarean section (CS).
followup_time: N/A (outcomes measured at birth and immediate neonatal period)
gest_age: Gestational age was a variable considered for patient subdivision, with a specific subgroup of 'greater than 40 weeks'.
